steps_as_read: A $100 — back to the original price [circled]

fingerprint.intervention: Have her predict then work out each stage in money: first add 50% of $100 to get the new price, then take 50% off that new price, and compare the two money amounts taken on and off.
fingerprint.misconception: successive percentage changes cancel by addition
fingerprint.reasoning: The student added +50% and -50% to get 0% and concluded the price stays at $100.

A.final_answer: A $100 — back to the original price

fingerprint.intervention: Have her first calculate $100 + 50% to get $150, then calculate 50% of $150 and compare that cash amount to the first $50 increase to see they are different.
fingerprint.reasoning: Adding +50% and -50% gives 0% so the price is unchanged at $100.

fingerprint.intervention: Have her predict then work out 50% up from $100 to get $150 and then 50% off that $150, and compare the take-off to the add-on to see the bases differ.
fingerprint.reasoning: Thinks +50% and -50% add to 0% so the price returns to $100.

fingerprint.intervention: Have her work it in two steps predicting first: what is $100 + 50%, then what is 50% of that new amount and subtract it to compare to $100.
fingerprint.reasoning: Thinks +50% and -50% add to 0% so the price stays at $100.

fingerprint.intervention: Have the student predict then work out 50% up from $100 to get $150, then work out 50% off that $150 and compare the dollar size of the two 50% amounts.
fingerprint.reasoning: Thought +50% and -50% add to 0% so the price stays at $100.

fingerprint.intervention: Have the student predict half of $150, work it out, and compare it to $150 minus $50 to see they are not the same.
fingerprint.reasoning: Student treated 50% as $50, adding $50 to get $150 then subtracting $50 to return to $100.

fingerprint.intervention: Have the student predict then shade 50% of a 100-bar and then 50% of the resulting 150-bar to see the second change is $75, not $50.
fingerprint.reasoning: Added $50 for the 50% increase and subtracted $50 for the 50% decrease, treating percent as a fixed dollar amount so they cancel.

fingerprint.intervention: Ask the student to predict then work out 50% of $150 using their method to see the decrease is $75 not $50, then compare the two percentage bases.
fingerprint.reasoning: Treated 50% as 50 dollars and added then subtracted it so the changes cancel to the original.

fingerprint.intervention: Have the student predict then work out 50% of $150 and compare it to 50% of $100 to see the decrease is larger than the increase.
fingerprint.reasoning: treated 50% as a fixed $50 amount that is added then subtracted, so the increase and decrease cancel back to $100.

fingerprint.intervention: Have the student work out what 50% of the new $150 actually is and predict whether taking that off can still leave $100.
fingerprint.misconception: percentage changes cancel as equal absolute amounts
fingerprint.reasoning: Treated both 50% changes as a fixed $50 added then subtracted, so they cancel back to $100.
